revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Bridge Engineering
revealWordProblem.text: The Golden Gate Bridge's two main cables are each about 7,650 feet long. A supply company sells cable-protection wrap in spools measured in yards. How many yards of protective wrap does one full cable need? Show your work using a conversion factor.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 1 yard = 3 feet, so converting feet to the larger unit (yards) means dividing by the conversion factor: 7,650 ÷ 3 = 2,550 yards. One cable needs 2,550 yards of protective wrap.

questions.stem: How many inches are in 7 feet?
choiceFeedback: There are 12 inches in every foot.
Multiply 7 by 12 (inches per foot).
You multiplied by 8 feet. Re-read how many feet the question gives.
hints: The key fact: 1 foot = 12 inches. You have 7 feet and want inches.
Going from a BIGGER unit (feet) to a SMALLER unit (inches) means you multiply.
Set up 7 × 12 — seven groups of 12 inches.
hintsEs: El dato clave: 1 pie = 12 pulgadas. Tienes 7 pies y quieres pulgadas.
Ir de una unidad MAYOR (pies) a una MENOR (pulgadas) significa que multiplicas.
Plantea 7 × 12: siete grupos de 12 pulgadas.

questions.stem: How many feet are in 3 yards?
choiceFeedback: Multiply 3 by 3 (feet per yard).
There are 3 feet in every yard.
Not quite. 1 yard = ___ feet.
hints: The key fact: 1 yard = 3 feet. You have 3 yards and want feet.
Big unit (yards) to small unit (feet) means multiply by the conversion factor 3.
Set up 3 × 3 — three yards, each worth 3 feet.
hintsEs: El dato clave: 1 yarda = 3 pies. Tienes 3 yardas y quieres pies.
De unidad grande (yardas) a unidad pequeña (pies) significa multiplicar por el factor de conversión 3.
Plantea 3 × 3: tres yardas, cada una de 3 pies.

questions.stem: How many ounces are in 4 pounds?
choiceFeedback: Not quite. 1 pound = ___ ounces.
There are 16 ounces in every pound.
Multiply 4 by 16 (ounces per pound).
hints: The key fact: 1 pound = 16 ounces. You have 4 pounds and want ounces.
Pounds are bigger than ounces, so converting to ounces means multiplying by 16.
Set up 4 × 16. (Break it up: 4 × 10 = 40 and 4 × 6 = 24, then add.)
hintsEs: El dato clave: 1 libra = 16 onzas. Tienes 4 libras y quieres onzas.
Las libras son mayores que las onzas, así que convertir a onzas significa multiplicar por 16.
Plantea 4 × 16. (Sepáralo: 4 × 10 = 40 y 4 × 6 = 24, y luego suma.)

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Convert Measurement Units is applying the conversion factor in the wrong direction — for example, converting 4 feet to inches by dividing (4 ÷ 12 = 0.33 inches) instead of multiplying (4 × 12 = 48 inches), or converting 80 ounces to pounds by multiplying (80 × 16 = 1,280 pounds) instead of dividing (80 ÷ 16 = 5 pounds). Before you answer, ask: am I changing to a SMALLER unit (there will be MORE of them, so multiply) or a BIGGER unit (there will be FEWER of them, so divide)?

level1.stem: (Lesson 3.4) Complete a new equivalent ratio: 2:3 = ___:___. Use a scale factor of 2.
hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
Use the visual model, then complete one step at a time.
Start like this: Multiply 2 × 2: 4.
level1.explanation: Multiply 2 × 2: 4. Multiply 3 × 2: 6. Write the equivalent ratio: 4:6.
level1.stemEs: Completa una nueva razón equivalente: 2:3 = ___:___. Usa un factor de escala de 2.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?

Empieza así: Multiplica 2 × 2: 4.
level1.explanationEs: Multiplica 2 × 2: 4. Multiplica 3 × 2: 6. Escribe la razón equivalente: 4:6.

level1.stem: (Lesson 3.5) Compare gold tiles per blue tile for 2:3 and 3:5. Which ratio gives fewer gold tiles per blue tile? Type first or second.

steps.prompt: The smaller rate belongs to the ___ ratio (type first or second).
steps.promptEs: La tasa menor corresponde a la razón ___ (escribe first o second).

hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
Use the visual model, then complete one step at a time.
Start like this: First rate — gold per blue: 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5.
level1.explanation: First rate — gold per blue: 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5. Second rate — gold per blue: 5 ÷ 3 = 1.6667. The smaller rate belongs to the first ratio (type first or second).
level1.stemEs: Compara las fichas doradas por cada ficha azul en 2:3 y 3:5. ¿Qué razón da menos fichas doradas por ficha azul? Escribe first (primera) o second (segunda).
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?
Usa el modelo visual y completa un paso a la vez.
Empieza así: Primera tasa — doradas por azul: 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5.
level1.explanationEs: Primera tasa — doradas por azul: 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5. Segunda tasa — doradas por azul: 5 ÷ 3 = 1.6667. La tasa menor corresponde a la razón first (escribe first o second).

choiceFeedback: Divide 24 by 12 (inches per foot).
There are 12 inches in one foot.
That is the number of inches. Going from inches to feet means dividing.
hints: This one goes the OTHER direction: inches (small) to feet (big), so the number of units gets smaller.

De unidad pequeña a unidad grande significa dividir. Pregunta: ¿cuántos grupos de 12 pulgadas caben en 24 pulgadas?
Plantea 24 ÷ 12.

level2.stem: 1 yard = 3 feet. Convert 9 yards to feet.
hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
feet are smaller than yards, so the number gets bigger — multiply.
Start like this: Each yard is worth 3 feet.
level2.stemEs: 1 yarda = 3 pies. Convierte 9 yardas a pies.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?
En pies el número será mayor que en yardas, así que multiplica.
Empieza así: Cada yarda equivale a 3 pies.

level2.stem: A shelf is 30 inches long. How many feet and inches is that?
choiceFeedback: 18 inches is more than a foot, so this answer is not finished. Keep taking out groups of 12 inches until fewer than 12 remain.
Find how many complete feet fit, then how many inches left over.
Divide by 12 and look for a remainder: 30 ÷ 12 = 2 R6.
hints: 30 inches is more than 2 feet (24 in) but less than 3 feet (36 in) — so the answer is 2 feet plus some leftover inches.
Divide by 12 to find whole feet; the REMAINDER stays as inches.
Compute 30 ÷ 12: it goes in 2 whole times using up 24 inches. Subtract 30 − 24 to find the leftover inches.
level2.stemEs: Un estante mide 30 pulgadas de largo. ¿A cuántos pies y pulgadas equivale?
level2.explanationEs: 30 ÷ 12 = 2 y sobran 6. Entonces 30 pulgadas = 2 pies 6 pulgadas.
hintsEs: 30 pulgadas es más de 2 pies (24 pulg) pero menos de 3 pies (36 pulg), así que la respuesta es 2 pies más unas pulgadas sobrantes.
Divide entre 12 para hallar los pies enteros; el RESIDUO se queda como pulgadas.
Calcula 30 ÷ 12: cabe 2 veces enteras usando 24 pulgadas. Resta 30 − 24 para hallar las pulgadas sobrantes.

level3.stem: Convert 3 hours to seconds using 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds.
choiceFeedback: That multiplies only two of the three numbers. Go hours to minutes to seconds: 3 x 60 x 60.
That is 3 hours converted to MINUTES. Convert once more: 180 minutes x 60 seconds per minute.
That is the number of seconds in ONE hour. Multiply by 3 for three hours.
level3.explanation: 3 hours × 60 minutes per hour = 180 minutes. Then 180 × 60 seconds per minute = 10,800 seconds.

level3.prompt: A recipe says you need 5 feet of ribbon, but the store only sells ribbon in inches. Another recipe says you need 2 yards of fabric, but your ruler measures in feet. Convert both measurements and explain the steps you used. Which conversion factor did you use each time?
level3.sentenceFrame: 5 feet = ___ inches because ___. 2 yards = ___ feet because ___. The conversion factors I used were ___.
level3.hint: First convert 5 feet to inches, then compare that total to the store's ribbon-selling unit.
hints: There are two separate conversions: 5 feet → inches, and 2 yards → feet. Each uses a different conversion factor.
Both go from a bigger unit to a smaller unit, so both are multiplication. Name the factor you use each time.
Start the ribbon: 5 × 12, since every foot holds 12 inches. Then the fabric: 2 × 3, since every yard holds 3 feet.
level3.explanation: Both conversions go from a bigger unit to a smaller one, so both multiply. Using 12 inches per foot, 5 × 12 = 60 inches of ribbon; using 3 feet per yard, 2 × 3 = 6 feet of fabric. Naming the conversion factor each time is what explains why both numbers grew.
level3.explanationEs: Las dos conversiones van de una unidad más grande a una más pequeña, así que ambas se multiplican. Con 12 pulgadas por pie, 5 × 12 = 60 pulgadas de cinta; con 3 pies por yarda, 2 × 3 = 6 pies de tela. Nombrar el factor de conversión cada vez es lo que explica por qué los dos números crecieron.
level3.promptEs: Una receta dice que necesitas 5 pies de listón, pero la tienda solo vende listón en pulgadas. Otra receta dice que necesitas 2 yardas de tela, pero tu regla mide en pies. Convierte las dos medidas y explica los pasos que usaste. ¿Qué factor de conversión usaste en cada caso?
hintsEs: Hay dos conversiones distintas: 5 pies → pulgadas y 2 yardas → pies. Cada una usa un factor de conversión diferente.
Ambas van de una unidad mayor a una menor, así que ambas son multiplicación. Nombra el factor que usas cada vez.
Empieza con el listón: 5 × 12, porque cada pie tiene 12 pulgadas. Luego la tela: 2 × 3, porque cada yarda tiene 3 pies.

predict.stem: Before you build the table — 1 foot is 12 inches. How many inches is 7 feet?
predict.explanation: Write 7 feet over 1 and multiply by 12 inches per 1 foot so feet cancel: 7 × 12 = 84 inches.
choiceFeedback: That applies the conversion in the wrong direction, dividing instead of multiplying. Inches are smaller, so there are MORE of them.
That adds 12 to 7 instead of multiplying.
That leaves the number unchanged. Changing the unit changes the number.
